incidents.name: Velocore ConstantProductPool fee underflow
incidents.notes: Velocore's ConstantProductPool computed its swap fee with an unchecked multiplier that overflows once a single withdrawal takes effectively the whole LP supply, so a flash-loaned burn of the USDC/ETH VLP returned far more than the pool held and drained it through the vault's execute path.

sources.ref: onchain review over a Linea archive RPC (linea-rpc.publicnode.com; the l2beat Linea endpoint does not serve 2024 blocks): the USDC/ETH VLP pool 0xe2c67A9B15e9E7FF8A9Cb0dFb8feE5609923E5DB was created at block 128549, 2023-08-05T05:24:29Z, by the Velocore factory deployer 0xca0671f5c50e4f28ae847480ee24cfe11c5c1b35, not the attack-tx sender 0x8cdc37ed79c5ef116b9dc2a53cb86acaca3716bf; cast logs finds no Upgraded event on the pool before the incident block 5079177 (2024-06-02T02:37:29Z), so the executing code was 301.7 days old. Swaps are routed through the Velocore vault 0x1d0188c4B276A09366D05d6Be06aF61a73bC7535. Loss ~$6.88M as previously recorded.
